Subject: Recommended engine slate + regression playbook (post-demo)

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and the recommended next steps from our side based on the demo and the sample request set you shared.

Summary of recommended engine slate (prioritized):
- Engine-A (4-bit quantized variant) — best cost/latency balance for high throughputs (≈3–6ms/token on our Dedicated pool); expected ~12–18% lower token cost vs Engine-B with comparable end-user quality for the Stratus support prompts.
- Engine-B (FP16) — highest quality for conversational nuance (better on long-context summarization tests); higher token latency (~8–12ms/token) and ~22% higher unit cost; recommend for your high-accuracy routing tier.
- Engine-C (compact distilled) — lowest latency, low-cost fallback for bursty traffic and short-answer flows where hallucination risk is acceptable.

Why this slate: your workload has two dominant paths — (1) high-frequency short replies for triage tickets and (2) occasional long-context summarization for incident post-mortems. The slate lets you route critical long-context work to Engine-B, keep day-to-day replies on Engine-A, and use Engine-C for cost-limited bursts.

Regression & monitoring playbook (summary):
- Eval harness: nightly runs against your 250 prompt regression set (included as prompt-sets-v1.md). Diff alerts when ROUGE/EM or our judgment score shifts > 3%.
- Canary rollout: 1% traffic for 24h with token-level tracing and sample retention; automatic rollback on latency p95 breach or quality regression threshold.
- Quality sampling: 200 human-review checks per week for first month; escalate to a model rollback if mean human rating drops > 0.4/5 compared to baseline.

Attachments sent: stratus-demo-benchmarks.csv (latency/cost/quality breakdown per engine), prompt-sets-v1.md (regression prompts + grading rubric). Full benchmark artifacts are in the Drive link below.

Proposed near-term action items:
1) Confirm which engine(s) you want in the initial pilot (Engine-A recommended default).
2) Approve the regression cadence and sample size (can tweak).
3) Schedule a 30-min ops sync this week to walk the canary and tracing setup (Ben/Karthik to lead).

If this looks good I can open a mutual action plan in HubSpot and loop in your procurement contact for the Dedicated capacity path.

Thanks —

2) The nightly evals — will those run on our private data only (in our VPC) or will Redwood run them in a hosted environment? We need to ensure no log/data leaves our environment for the first 90 days.
3) Procurement question: do you have a standard MSA + addendum for Dedicated capacity? I cc'd procurement for next steps.

Also: curious about the human-review process — do you provide the UI + reviewer pool or do we need to supply raters?

If possible let's target a short ops sync tomorrow afternoon (Alicia time) — can you propose 1–2 slots?

Alicia —

Quick answers to the items you raised: 
- 3–6ms/token is median (p50) measured on our Dedicated 8xA100 pool with the 4-bit quantized Engine-A. p95 tends to be ~2.5x p50 depending on sequence length; for short-reply distributions we'd expect p95 in the ~60–130ms range for token generation alone. End-to-end depends on network and prefix processing but we've shipped setups that meet your 150ms p95 with batching disabled and the routing layer pinned.
- Regression evals: runs can be configured to execute entirely in your VPC (we provide a containerized harness), or we can run hosted copies if you prefer. For the pilot we'll default to VPC-only.
- MSA/process: we have a Dedicated capacity addendum we can share; Marissa has the procurement checklist and I'll coordinate commercial terms once you confirm pilot engines.
- Human review: we can provide a managed QA UI and access to our vetted rater pool under NDA, or you can run reviews internally. For speed during pilot we usually provide the rater service and share labels back to the customer.

I'll be on the ops sync; propose 2:30pm–3:00pm PT tomorrow or 11:00am–11:30am PT if you prefer earlier.
